files.README.md:
# Media and camera wall
All connections are optional. Bind an existing Plex/Jellyfin/Emby-compatible integration for native now-playing sessions. Bind an HTTP camera snapshot server and configure up to eight name/path entries for authenticated JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/AVIF still images. This is snapshot polling, not RTSP or continuous video streaming.

For Immich, bind the server root URL and keep `x-api-key` in the local connection's secret headers. The key needs asset.read and asset.view. The package lists recent image assets through POST /api/search/metadata and retrieves each thumbnail through GET /api/assets/:id/thumbnail?size=thumbnail. Each image is fetched server-side; credentials are never sent to the browser. Each image is limited to 675 KiB before base64 encoding. If an endpoint redirects, configure a direct image endpoint supported by your service.

Tile and advanced views share the selected image. Clicking a thumbnail opens the advanced view; the media session panel retains playback progress and native session details. Images refresh independently, so one failed camera does not hide the others. The package does not promise lossless full-resolution originals or real-time video.

Official API sources: https://github.com/immich-app/immich/blob/main/server/src/controllers/search.controller.ts and https://github.com/immich-app/immich/blob/main/server/src/controllers/asset-media.controller.ts

camera.label: Camera snapshot server
camera.description: Basic, bearer or header authentication stays in this local connection.

immich.label: Immich server
immich.description: Use a secret x-api-key header with asset.read and asset.view permissions.

cameras.label: Camera snapshots
cameras.description: Array of name/path objects on the camera connection. Up to eight snapshots. Paths stay on that connection’s origin.
